### 4b. The wall-clock column is CONFOUNDED — slot-pool occupancy

The arms ran in order A, B, C, and R13 gives every cell a fresh never-reused slot, so arm order is also slot-index order and pool-occupancy order. This CONTROL re-runs the SHIPPED layout (arm A, unchanged) at the high slot indices arm C used, on cells arm A already ran at low indices. Server-reported prefill and decode are the comparison's own control: they are flat while wall is not.

| run | layout | slots | n | median wall s | median prefill ms | median decode ms | median tokens_out | FALSE-POS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| grid (early) | A | 28–35 | 72 | **1.15** | 572.45 | 537.3 | 29.5 | 24/24 (100%) |
| control (late) | A | 100–103 | 36 | **5.02** | 561.3 | 553.1 | 30.0 | 12/12 (100%) |

So the per-arm wall-clock in §4 prices the slot index, not the layout, and it is reported here rather than deleted. What the layout actually costs is TOKENS, which are exact: see the head column in §2 and the `tokens_in` column in §4.

# Findings

Run 2026-08-14, branch `capa1`, suite green (479 tests). Leaf:
`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M` on ROCm, launched exactly as §4/S0 specify
(`-np 128 -c 327680 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -ub 512 -b 2048 -lm none
--no-kv-unified --cont-batching`, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=1`), one process for
the whole experiment, shut down after. **777 real leaf calls**: 153
replication, 576 grid, 12 cache probe, 36 latency control — plus 8 recorded
`inadmissible` cells (arm B at 2,048, §4). Every number below comes from a
record in `milestones/s2/results/distance.jsonl`.

`prompts/leaf-prefix.v1.md` was used **verbatim in all three arms** and was not
edited. The only variable in FACTOR 1 is where those bytes sit.

---

## 0. THE HEADLINE

1. **The 30/30 → 0/21 result replicates exactly** (p = 8.74e-15), on the same
   documents, under the same prefix, in a fresh process.
2. **It is DISTANCE, not density.** At a fixed 3 entity bindings, the
   false-positive rate goes 0/12 at 640 tokens to 12/12 at 1,024
   (p = 7.4e-07). At fixed size, doubling or nearly quadrupling the distractor
   bindings moves it by **nothing at all**: 0/12 vs 0/12 at 640, 12/12 vs 12/12
   at 1,024, 12/12 vs 12/12 at 2,048 — three p = 1.0's. The §4 INSTRUCTION
   DECAY hypothesis survives the experiment designed to kill it.
3. **But the layout fix is not a fix.** Both treatments cut false positives to
   ~2% (p = 4.2e-08) and both pay for it in recall (B 57%, C 65% vs A 83%;
   p = 1.3e-04 and 4.9e-03), and the payment is exactly the pathology this
   experiment was pre-registered to catch: MISS goes 9% → 40% (B) and 32% (C).
   At 2,048 tokens arm C posts **0/24 false positives and 0/48 recall** — it
   refuses every question, present or absent. That is a failure, reported as
   one.
4. **At 640 tokens all three layouts are equal** (0/12 false positives, 24/24
   literal recall). The distance fix makes the layout question moot; the layout
   fix does not make the distance question moot.

**Recommendation: do not change the layout in `config.yaml`.** Keep
`[system prefix][chunk][question]`. The costs of the alternatives are stated in
§4 below, but the decisive point is §0.4: nothing the layout buys at 1,024 is
worth having, and at 640 there is nothing left to buy.

---

## 1. Replication

30/30 at 1,024 vs 0/21 at 640, against `milestones/s2/REFUSAL-AB.md`'s 30/30 vs 0/21. The
sub-tables replicate too, not just the headline: literal 27/30 vs 21/21,
paraphrase 24/30 vs 14/21, MISS 0/60 vs 6/42, one MALFORMED at 1,024. This is
the same measurement, in a new process, on fresh slots, and it is stable.

## 2. Distance vs density — the verdict

**Distance is the cause. Density is not a factor.**

| arm A, false positives | 640 | 1,024 | 2,048 |
|---|---|---|---|
| matched density (3 bindings at every size) | **0/12** | **12/12** | **12/12** |
| natural density (3 / 6 / 11 bindings) | 0/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |

Reading across the top row: with the entity inventory held constant and the
extra length made of entity-free filler, the rate goes from floor to ceiling
between 640 and 1,024 tokens. Reading down each column: at constant length,
doubling (1,024) or nearly quadrupling (2,048) the number of competing
entity–identifier bindings changes nothing. The confound `milestones/s2/REFUSAL-AB.md` §2
flagged, and which §4 called the reason not to act, is dead — it was never
carrying the effect.

Two supporting observations, both from arm A:

* The ABSENT question has no needle, so its failure cannot be a
  needle-retrieval failure. What varies across the top row is the number of
  tokens between the instructions and the point of generation, and those tokens
  carry no identifiers at all (asserted at build time against
  `rlm.leakcheck`'s own pattern set).
* The **fact**-distance cliff lands in the same place in the same run: arm A
  literal recall is 24/24 at 640 and at 1,024 and collapses to 12/24 (plus 11
  confabulations) at 2,048, where the 50%-depth needle sits ~1,024 tokens from
  the question. §7 #2's cliff and this false-positive cliff are at the same
  distance, in one experiment, with density controlled. That is the "same
  phenomenon measured twice" claim, now supported rather than conjectured.

## 3. What the layout arms actually did

false-positives · literal recall · paraphrase recall, per size (n = 24 each):

| | 640 | 1,024 | 2,048 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** shipped | 0/24 · 24/24 · 13/24 | 24/24 · 24/24 · 19/24 | 24/24 · 12/24 · 0/24 |
| **B** repeated | 0/24 · 24/24 · 15/24 | 1/24 · 15/24 · 1/24 | INADMISSIBLE |
| **C** after | 0/24 · 24/24 · 16/24 | 1/24 · 19/24 · 3/24 | 0/24 · 0/24 · 0/24 |

Moving the instructions next to the question does exactly what the hypothesis
predicts to the ABSENT column — and it moves the whole decision boundary with
it. At 1,024, arm B turns 23 of 24 absent questions into clean `NONE`s and
turns 23 of 24 **paraphrase** questions into `NONE` as well. The model did not
become more accurate; it became more willing to refuse, and the refusals land
on present facts at nearly the same rate. Arm C at 2,048 is the reductio: 48/48
MISS, every answer the literal string `NONE`, at a 0% false-positive rate that
means nothing.

This is why the false-positive rate was never allowed to be reported alone.

One honest limitation of holding the wording fixed: `leaf-prefix.v1.md` says
"the user message is the excerpt, then a blank line, then the question", which
is no longer literally true in B and C, where instruction text sits inside the
user message. Rewriting it would have made position and wording move together,
which is the one thing this design forbids — so the mismatch is a cost of the
control, and a prefix authored FOR a post-chunk position is a different
experiment, not a free improvement on this one.

## 4. The price, stated exactly

* **Tokens (exact, and the number to plan with).** The rendered head is 311
  tokens for A and C and **616 for B** — the repeated prefix costs +305 tokens
  on every call, +22% of a 1,024-window prompt (1,686 vs 1,382 `tokens_in`).
* **Slot capacity (a hard stop, not a cost curve).** At the pinned
  `-np 128 -c 327680` = 2,560 tokens/slot, arm B **cannot run a 2,048-token
  window at all**: 616 + 2,048 + question > 2,560. Eight of its cells are
  recorded `inadmissible` rather than quietly dropped. A layout that forbids
  window sizes the runtime may want is a bad trade for an effect that is not a
  fix.
* **§4's cache contract is worth less than §4 assumes, for a reason that
  predates this experiment.** Under R13's never-reuse policy every window gets
  a virgin slot, so the byte-identical leading prefix is re-prefilled for every
  window whatever the layout; the thing it could buy — a second document
  landing on a slot that already holds the prefix — is a pattern the runtime is
  forbidden to use. Intra-window re-query, the reuse that actually pays
  (§7 #3 (d)), survives in all three layouts, because the chunk is still the
  first byte of the user message in every one of them.
* **`tokens_cached` could not price it, and that is its own finding (§10 R8).**
  The cache probe ran twice. In replicate 1 the second document reported
  `cache_n` 0 / 866 / 879 (A/B/C); in replicate 2, with the true shared prefix
  measured on the same server immediately before each call, it reported
  1,378 / 1,682 / 1,374 with prefill collapsing to ~50 ms — **against a true
  shared token prefix of 311, 311 and 3.** Layout C cannot reuse 1,374 tokens
  of a document with which it shares 3. Both replicates returned the
  document-correct key, so the leaf demonstrably read the document it was asked
  about; it is the instrument that is wrong, and in both directions (within a
  cell it *under*-reports: ~880 where ~1,335 tokens are genuinely shared).
  **§7 #3's token-weighted gates rest on this field and should be re-derived on
  this build before they price anything.**

## 5. A second finding nobody was looking for: latency scales with slot-pool occupancy

Median wall for identical work — same layout, same cells, same server-reported
prefill and decode: **1.15 s at slots 28–35, 5.02 s at slots 100–103** (§4b).
`timings` are flat across that 4.4× (prefill 572 → 561 ms, decode 537 → 553 ms,
`tokens_out` 29.5 → 30), so the time is spent outside the numbers the trace
records. The arms ran A, B, C in slot order, so **every per-arm wall-clock in
this report is confounded by it** and none of it is attributable to layout —
which the control establishes rather than assumes.

This matters beyond this experiment. R13's never-reuse policy consumes slots
monotonically through an episode, so if the effect is occupancy-driven,
per-call latency degrades as an episode proceeds and a 261-window corpus spends
most of its life at the slow end. `milestones/s2/R13-slotcount.md` priced `-np 128` on
memory and on aggregate prefill; it did not measure this. **Pre-registered
follow-up: sweep call latency against occupied-slot count at a fixed prompt,
and re-price the rotation policy against the answer.**

## 6. What to do instead, and what it costs

The lever is geometry, and this run brackets it: the false-positive cliff sits
between **640 and 1,024** tokens of instruction-to-generation distance, the
same bracket §7 #2 measured for facts ([967 pass, 1022 fail]). `config.yaml`
ships `window 1024 / stride 768` — **the window is on the wrong side of the
cliff**, and this run prices that: 24/24 false positives at 1,024 versus 0/24
at 640, with literal recall identical at both (24/24) and paraphrase recall the
one thing 640 gives up (13/24 vs 19/24).

That is a config change with a real budget consequence, and it is NOT made
here: window 640 / stride 480 turns a 200K-token corpus from 261 windows into
417, and at 2 questions per window that is 834 sub-calls against
`max_subcalls: 522` — the budget breaks before the corpus does. Re-deriving the
window therefore has to be a joint decision with §8's corpus-size ceiling and
C5's budgets, on its own pre-registered run, with the paraphrase-recall loss at
640 measured rather than assumed.

**So: `config.yaml` layout unchanged; `scaffold.chunk.size_tokens` flagged for
re-derivation with the arithmetic above attached.** The negative result — the
fix the architecture note proposed trades false positives for misses roughly
one-for-one — is published rather than tuned away, per §10 R1.
